messages.subject: Showing values in bar chart
parts:
Could You please give an example - how one can add values into bar
charts?
I did not found any example
neither in documentation (http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_text.html;
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_bar.html)
nor in book "ggplot2".
I am interested to know how one can add values into bars into books
"ggplot2" figure 4.8 (b):

library(ggplot2)
dplot = ggplot(diamonds, aes(clarity, fill = cut))
dplot + geom_bar(position = "fill")
... # adding values (in range [0,1]) for each bar by each value of
variable "clarity" with geom_text() ?

Best regards,
Jüri

messages.author: 424f4fd55acd5d2d
messages.subject: Re: Showing values in bar chart
parts:
Hi Jüri,

I've ran in to the same issue myself. I've not found an easy way other than to create a second data set which contains the x and y position of the labels along with the text to print. For the example you have included I would do something like this:



library(ggplot2)
dplot <- ggplot(diamonds, aes(clarity, fill = cut)) +
    geom_bar(position = "fill")

# cross tabulate the two variables of interest
xt <- table(diamonds$cut, diamonds$clarity)
# turn counts in to column proportions
xt <- prop.table(xt, margin = 2)
# xt is the information we want to print, however we need to calculate
# where we want to print

# start by calculating the cumulative proportions (the tops of each of the bars)
cum.xt <- xt
for (m in 2:nrow(cum.xt)) {
    cum.xt[m, ] <- cum.xt[m-1, ] + cum.xt[m, ]
}

# calculate the midpoints in each of the bars, these will be the label positions
label.positions <- xt

for (m in 2:nrow(label.positions)) {
    label.positions[m, ] <- cum.xt[m-1, ] + xt[m, ] / 2
}

label.positions[1, ] <- label.positions[1,] / 2

# to keep things tidy collect all this information in to a data frame
xt <- melt(xt)
xt$value <- round(xt$value, 2)
label.positions <- melt(label.positions)

my.labels <- data.frame(x = xt$Var.2, y = label.positions$value,
    label = xt$value)

# finally, add the labels to dplot
dplot + geom_text(data = my.labels, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label))

# but as you can see there's not enough room for the categories
# with small proportions so let's remove them
my.labels <- subset(my.labels, label > 0.025)

# add a bit of transparency to the text and change the colour to white
# so it does not distract readers from the actual graphic
dplot + geom_text(data = my.labels, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
    alpha = 0.6, colour = "white")



Cheers

Stu
